SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: champion = LPD-combine W=4 + FILTERED-DC (single fbp(Rx-g)) K=30, 5-seed mean 0.4590+-0.0294 @ 183p (best 0.5047). Filtered-DC uses ONE filtered gradient per step; a proper CG solve of the normal equations is a MUCH stronger DC solver -- CG-DC is the mechanism that got fastdiff-pixel-DC-on to 0.52 and wavelet-DC-on to 0.28. UNTESTED in this unroll. (2) FAILURE MODE: a single filtered gradient only partially enforces Rx=g each step; 30 of them approximate consistency but a per-step CG solve nails it far better. (3) ONE KNOB (architectural): dc_mode 'filtered'->'cg' -- I added CGDataConsistency: n_cg=5 matrix-free CG iterations solving (R^T R + lam I)d = R^T(g - Rx) for the DC update d (lam = softplus(learnable), damps the ill-conditioned 128-view normal operator), fed to the SAME LPD-combine block. +1 param (lam) -> 184 total. NOT byte-for-byte the champion (CG is a different, stronger DC operator) -- it is a genuine architectural swap of the DC solver. (4) HYPOTHESIS: a per-step CG least-squares DC solve enforces Rx=g much more completely than one filtered gradient, so the LPD-combine routes a cleaner, more consistent correction -> hr climbs past 0.5047 toward the 0.52-0.63 regime (fastdiff CG-DC reached 0.52). Risk: CG on the ill-conditioned 128-view operator can amplify streaks if underdamped -> lam is learnable to control this. (5) BUDGET: 5 CG iters = 5 fwd+back-proj PAIRS per unroll step x K=30 -> ~10x the projector calls of filtered-DC; may only fit a few epochs in 1080s -- if hr promising but undertrained, iter-26 reduces cg_n or K. train_n=200, --time=00:30:00, 200-val, 20-min budget. (6) SERIAL; iter-26: tune cg_n/lam if it helps, then multi-scale-bilateral POST-filter., dc_mode=cg, per_step_alpha=True, lpd_on=True, lpd_width=4, lpd_kernel=3, anisotropic_on_top=False, cg_n=5, cg_lam_init=0.01
